mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW Z4 35i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW Z4 35i engine replacement typically costs £2,500-£5,500 supply-only for a reconditioned or rebuilt N54B30. Fitted by a specialist, expect £4,000-£7,500 total. Used N54B30 engines: £1,500-£2,800 supply-only from UK breakers. Reconditioned N54B30: £2,500-£4,200 supply-only. Rebuilt N54B30: £3,500-£5,500 supply-only. Professional fitting adds £1,200-£2,000 depending on your location and workshop.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of HPFP failure in a BMW Z4 35i N54 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: HPFP failure is the most notorious issue on the N54 engine. Symptoms include long cranking times before the engine starts, illumination of the 'Service Engine Soon' warning light, and reduced (safe-mode) engine performance. Long cranking at start-up is the classic symptom. Loss of power under load or at high RPM. Engine malfunction warning light. In some cases, complete engine shutdown while driving.  Warning: Ignoring HPFP symptoms can lead to complete engine shutdown while driving - a potential safety hazard.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW Z4 35i N54 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N54B30 is a high-performance engine that delivers exceptional power, but it has well-documented reliability concerns. The Z4 35i can generate multiple expensive failures. HPFP failure is the most common issue - budget for replacement. Fuel injectors can fail, causing misfires and rough idle. Turbocharger wastegate rattle is common on higher-mileage examples. Regular maintenance and preventative component replacement are essential. Many owners report engine replacements well under 100,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a high-mileage BMW Z4 35i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Z4 35i worth £8,000-£18,000, engine replacement (£3,500-£5,500 supply-only) can make financial sense if the body and interior are in good condition. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable up to roughly 60-70% of the car's value. For a well-maintained example with low mileage, replacement is usually justified. Low-mileage, rust-free, or cherished Z4 35i examples justify the investment. Always factor the 12-month warranty into your decision.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW Z4 35i N54 engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N54 engine's lifespan depends heavily on maintenance and component replacement. With proper care, 120,000-150,000 miles is achievable, but HPFP and injector failures often occur between 50,000-80,000 miles. HPFP typically fails between 50,000-80,000 miles. Injectors may require replacement around 50,000-80,000 miles. Turbo wastegate rattle often appears from 60,000-100,000 miles. Regular oil changes (every 8,000-10,000 miles) and using premium fuel extend engine life.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW Z4 35i engine with a standard Z4 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Swapping a Z4 35i's N54 twin-turbo for a naturally aspirated engine (N52) is technically possible but requires extensive modifications and is rarely cost-effective. Engine mounts, wiring loom, ECU, cooling system, and exhaust are all different. The N54's twin-turbo system requires specific cooling and oil supply. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Stick to like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage and straightforward installation.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW Z4 35i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW Z4 35i was launched in 2009 as the performance flagship of the E89 Z4 range, powered by the N54B30 - BMW's first mass-produced turbocharged petrol engine since the 1980s. Featuring twin-turbocharging and direct injection, the 3.0-litre straight-six produced 306hp and 400Nm of torque, delivering explosive performance in the retractable-hardtop roadster.

milestones.description: N54B30A, 3.0L twin-turbo petrol, 306hp - launch of the E89 Z4 sDrive35i
2016 - N54B30 continued, 306hp - production of the sDrive35i across the E89 generation
N54B30O0 variant code introduced - minor ECU calibration changes
End of E89 Z4 production; sDrive35i replaced by G29 M40i with B58 engine

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW Z4 35i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW Z4 35i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW Z4 35i's N54 twin-turbo straight-six is a landmark engine - BMW's first mass-produced turbo petrol since the 1980s - delivering exceptional performance. However, the N54 is notorious for expensive failures. High-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure, fuel injector failure, and turbocharger wastegate rattle are the most common issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded HPFP components, injectors and turbo hardware addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure - Why the BMW Z4 35i N54 Fails to Start
problems.rootCause: The HPFP is notorious for failing in the N54 engine. Internal plungers wear out of tolerance, starving direct injectors under load. Symptoms include long cranking times at engine start, illumination of the "Service Engine Soon" warning light, and reduced (safe-mode) engine performance. In some cases, it can cause complete engine shutdown.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace high-pressure fuel pump (part no. ending -943), fuel system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; resolves long cranking and performance issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace HPFP, all six fuel injectors, high-pressure fuel lines
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if injectors are also contaminated or failing

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N54 with upgraded HPFP and injectors; 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if fuel contamination has caused internal engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Z4 35i (2009-2016) is worth approximately £8,000-£18,000 depending on condition and mileage. HPFP replacement at a specialist (£700-£1,200) is a manageable repair on a vehicle of this value. Full engine replacement (£3,500-£5,500 supply-only) typically represents 20-50% of the vehicle's value - making it a significant but often justifiable investment for a well-maintained example.
problems.recommendation: The HPFP is the N54's Achilles' heel. If you experience long cranking times or reduced power, have the HPFP diagnosed immediately. BMW extended the warranty on HPFP and turbo wastegates on many N54 vehicles, but this may not cover all Z4 35i examples. Specialist replacement is typically 30-40% cheaper than main dealer pricing. On higher-mileage Z4 35i models, we recommend replacing both the HPFP and injectors together - individual component replacement often triggers secondary failures within 12 months.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N54B30 BMW Z4 35i engine prices

problems.h4: Fuel Injector Failure - Why the BMW Z4 35i N54 Misfires and Idles Roughly
problems.rootCause: The N54's piezo direct injectors can fail due to carbon buildup, internal wear, or electrical faults. Symptoms include rough idling, misfires, decreased fuel efficiency, and cold start issues. The Z4 35i can develop intermittent misfires requiring injector replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty injector, code to ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only one injector has failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all six fuel injectors, fuel system flush, ECU coding
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended on high-mileage N54; prevents multiple failures

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N54 with new injectors and HPFP; 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if injector failure has caused cylinder wall damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Injector replacement at a specialist (£1,200-£1,800 for all six) is a significant but manageable repair.
problems.recommendation: If your Z4 35i develops cold start issues or misfires, have the injectors inspected immediately. Replacing all six injectors at once is recommended on higher-mileage examples - individual replacement often leads to subsequent failures. Use only OEM or BMW-approved injectors - aftermarket units can cause further issues.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW Z4 35i injector repair and engine replacement quotes

problems.h4: Turbocharger Wastegate Rattle - Why the BMW Z4 35i N54 Rattles on Deceleration
problems.rootCause: The N54's turbocharger wastegates develop excessive movement between the wastegate and the wastegate seat, producing a characteristic rattle on deceleration. BMW extended the warranty on turbocharger wastegates to 8 years or 82,000 miles on some models.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if rattle is mild and turbo is otherwise sound

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove turbos, rebuild with new wastegates, bearings and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if rattle is severe or boost loss is present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N54 with upgraded turbos; 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo failure has contaminated the engine with metal debris

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Wastegate actuator replacement at a specialist (£500-£900) is a modest repair. Turbocharger rebuild remains a significant investment.
problems.recommendation: Wastegate rattle on the Z4 35i should not be ignored - it precedes actuator seizure and potential turbo failure. A specialist actuator replacement is highly effective for early-stage symptoms. Check if your vehicle is covered under the BMW wastegate warranty before paying for repairs. Once boost loss or check engine lights appear, a full turbo rebuild or replacement is typically required.
